sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在节目中，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上光怪陆离、奇妙有趣的事物，同时还能提高英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊Hannibal。

sentences.en: He was the Carthaginian general who marched on Rome, is remembered as one of the greatest tacticians in military history, and almost destroyed Rome two hundred years before it could declare itself an Empire.
sentences.zh: 他是率领军队进军罗马的迦太基将军，被公认为军事史上最伟大的战术家之一，在罗马自立为帝国的前两百年，他差点就将其彻底摧毁。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get started, and talk about Hannibal: Rome’s Greatest Enemy.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们开始吧，来聊聊Hannibal：罗马最伟大的敌人。

sentences.en: There are lots of promises you might have made as a child.
sentences.zh: 你小时候可能许下过许多承诺。

sentences.en: A promise to your parents that you’d always tidy your room, or that if you got a dog, you would always take it out for a walk, even if it was raining.
sentences.zh: 比如向父母保证会永远整理房间，或者如果养了狗，哪怕下雨也一定会带它出去遛弯。

sentences.en: Maybe it was a promise to a best friend that you’d be best friends forever, or a promise to a first girlfriend or boyfriend that nothing would ever come between you.
sentences.zh: 也许是向最好的朋友保证要做一辈子的死党，或是对初恋承诺你们之间永远不会有第三者。

sentences.en: Now, most children–and I’d have to include myself in this category–are not so good at keeping promises.
sentences.zh: 然而，大多数孩子——我得把我自己也归入这一类——都不太擅长兑现承诺。

sentences.en: Life happens, we change, and after all, it wasn’t that important in the first place.
sentences.zh: 生活总在变化，我们也在成长，而且说实话，最初这些承诺也没那么重要。

sentences.en: But for one young boy, a promise made before his tenth birthday would be something he would spend his entire life consumed by.
sentences.zh: 但对于一个年轻的男孩来说，他在十岁生日前许下的一个承诺，却成了他终其一生都为之痴迷的执念。

sentences.en: According to one legend, this nine-year-old swore to forever be an enemy of Rome, or to put it more precisely, he was forced to say, “I swear so soon as age will permit...I will use fire and steel to arrest the destiny of Rome.”
sentences.zh: 根据一个传说，这个九岁的男孩发誓要永远与罗马为敌，说得更精确一点，他被迫说出了这样的话：“我发誓，只要年龄允许……我将使用血与火来阻断罗马的命运。”

sentences.en: The boy’s name was Hannibal. Now, to understand why a father might make his child swear eternal hatred towards another state, we need to look at the world Hannibal was born into.
sentences.zh: 这个男孩名叫Hannibal。现在，为了理解为什么一个父亲会要求自己的孩子发誓对另一个国家永世为敌，我们需要看看Hannibal出生的那个世界。

sentences.en: He was born in 247 BCE in Carthage, in modern-day Tunisia.
sentences.zh: 他于公元前247年出生于迦太基，即今天的突尼斯。

sentences.en: At this time, Carthage was the heart of a strong maritime power.
sentences.zh: 在当时，迦太基是一个强大海上强国的核心。

sentences.en: Its navy dominated the western Mediterranean, its harbours were filled with goods from across North Africa, southern Spain, Sicily, even as far as the British Isles.
sentences.zh: 它的海军称霸西地中海，港口里停满了来自北非、西班牙南部、西西里岛，甚至远至不列颠群岛的货物。

sentences.en: Its strength came primarily from sea trade.
sentences.zh: 它的实力主要来源于海上贸易。

sentences.en: Rome, on the other hand, was mainly land-based.
sentences.zh: 与此相对，罗马主要是一个依靠陆地的国家。

sentences.en: At this point, in the late third century BCE, it wasn’t yet the mighty empire you’re probably picturing.
sentences.zh: 在公元前三世纪后期，它还不是你脑海中想象的那个强大帝国。

sentences.en: It was a regional republic with control over much of the Italian peninsula.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个控制了意大利半岛大部分地区的区域性共和国。

sentences.en: But many of the towns and cities it had “brought into the fold” were resentful.
sentences.zh: 但它“纳入版图”的许多城镇和城市都心怀怨恨。

sentences.en: Some had been defeated in battle and forced into uneasy alliances.
sentences.zh: 其中一些在战斗中被击败，被迫结成了勉强的同盟。

sentences.en: Others had been diplomatically absorbed, sucked up by this increasingly dominant power.
sentences.zh: 另一些则是通过外交手段被吞并，被这个日益主导的强权所蚕食。

sentences.en: The term “Rome” at this point meant a powerful, rising state, but not an empire.
sentences.zh: 此时的“罗马”意味着一个强大且正在崛起的国家，但还不是一个帝国。

sentences.en: Not yet, at least.
sentences.zh: 至少当时还不是。

sentences.en: This all changed with a war that came to be called the First Punic War.
sentences.zh: 这一切随着后来被称为第一次布匿战争的冲突而改变了。

sentences.en: It began in 264 BCE as a struggle for control over Sicily, the large, wealthy island that sat between Italy and North Africa.
sentences.zh: 这场战争始于公元前264年，是为了争夺西西里岛的控制权——那是位于意大利和北非之间的一座面积巨大、物产丰富的岛屿。

sentences.en: It was under the control of Carthage, but Rome wanted it for itself.
sentences.zh: 它原本在迦太基的控制之下，但罗马想要将它据为己有。

sentences.en: What followed was a brutal, 23-year conflict.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一场残酷且长达23年的冲突。

sentences.en: Rome had no navy to speak of when it began, but it built one from scratch.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发时，罗马几乎没有海军，但他们从零开始打造了一支。

sentences.en: Carthage, the great naval power, was pushed back, humiliated, and eventually forced to sign a peace treaty that saw it lose Sicily and pay heavy reparations.
sentences.zh: 迦太基这个伟大的海军强国被打退、羞辱，最终被迫签署了一份和平条约，不仅失去了西西里岛，还支付了巨额赔偿金。

sentences.en: It was embarrassing and expensive. And it wasn’t only the loss of territory that was problematic.
sentences.zh: 这既丢脸又昂贵。而且成问题的不只是领土的丧失。

sentences.en: Carthage tended to rely on mercenaries –paid-for soldiers–and at the end of the war, there were tens of thousands of these mercenaries who hadn’t been paid and were saying, “Where’s our money?”.
sentences.zh: 迦太基历来依赖雇佣兵——也就是拿钱办事的士兵——战争结束时，有数万名这样的雇佣兵没有拿到薪水，他们质问：“我们的钱呢？”

sentences.en: Carthage didn’t have the means to pay, the mercenaries rose up, and there was a violent rebellion that almost destroyed the city.
sentences.zh: 迦太基没有资金支付，雇佣兵们随即暴动，引发了一场差点摧毁整座城市的暴力叛乱。

sentences.en: During all of this chaos, Rome snuck in and also took the Mediterranean islands of Sardinia and Corsica.
sentences.zh: 正是在这片混乱中，罗马趁虚而入，顺势夺取了地中海的撒丁岛和科西嘉岛。

sentences.en: Now, that is a very brief summary, but it’s in the aftermath of these twin humiliations, defeat abroad and chaos at home, that we find Hamilcar Barca, Hannibal’s father.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个非常简短的概述，但正是在这两重羞辱——海外战败和国内混乱——的余波中，我们看到了Hannibal的父亲Hamilcar Barca。

sentences.en: He was a talented general and a proud Carthaginian, and, perhaps reasonably, he blamed Rome for all of this.
sentences.zh: 他是一位才华横溢的将军，也是一个骄傲的迦太基人，或许也算合情合理，他将这一切都归咎于罗马。

sentences.en: In his eyes, it was Rome that had dragged Carthage into a ruinous war.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，正是罗马把迦太基拖入了这场毁灭性的战争。

sentences.en: It was Rome that had crippled Carthaginian power and taken advantage of its internal disarray.
sentences.zh: 正是罗马削弱了迦太基的实力，并利用其内乱落井下石。

sentences.en: So, when Hamilcar set off to rebuild Carthaginian influence in Spain, where the silver mines were rich and the terrain made it an ideal place to train troops and launch future campaigns, he took his son Hannibal with him.
sentences.zh: 因此，当Hamilcar动身前往西班牙重建迦太基的影响力时——那里银矿丰富，地形也是训练军队和发动未来战役的理想地点——他带上了自己的儿子Hannibal。

sentences.en: And before they left, so the legend goes, he made Hannibal swear that he would never be Rome’s friend.
sentences.zh: 传闻说，在他们出发前，他让Hannibal发誓永远不做罗马的朋友。

sentences.en: Hannibal was a man–or boy at that time–who clearly kept his promises.
sentences.zh: Hannibal是一个——或者说当时还是个孩子——真正信守承诺的人。

sentences.en: And it would be in the Iberian Peninsula–in modern day Spain–that he would learn the skills that turned him into such a formidable military commander.
sentences.zh: 正是在伊比利亚半岛——也就是今天的西班牙——他学会了让他成长为一名令人生畏的军事统帅的各种技能。

sentences.en: Like Alexander the Great, who grew up under the watchful eye of his father, Philip of Macedon, Hannibal spent his youth in military camps, on campaign, learning not from books but from battlefields.
sentences.zh: 就像在父亲马其顿的腓力注视下长大的亚历山大大帝一样，Hannibal的青少年时期是在军营和战火中度过的，他的知识不是从书本上学来的，而是来自战场。

sentences.en: He saw sieges, skirmishes, the management of supplies and morale.
sentences.zh: 他目睹了围城战、小规模冲突以及补给和士气的管理。

sentences.en: By his late teens, he was already commanding men.
sentences.zh: 在他快二十岁时，他已经开始指挥部下了。

sentences.en: He had no formal schooling; his education was war.
sentences.zh: 他没有受过正规教育，他的教育就是战争。

sentences.en: After the death of his father and then his brother-in-law, Hannibal took command of Carthage’s forces in Iberia.
sentences.zh: 在父亲和姐夫相继去世后，Hannibal接管了迦太基在伊比利亚的军队。

sentences.en: He was only 26 years old, but he would prove to be more than capable.
sentences.zh: 他当时只有26岁，但他证明了自己完全能够胜任。

sentences.en: He was charismatic, brave, and cool under pressure.
sentences.zh: 他充满魅力、勇敢无畏，而且在压力面前冷静沉着。

sentences.en: His men loved him. His enemies feared him.
sentences.zh: 他的士兵爱戴他，他的敌人畏惧他。

sentences.en: And he was a master tactician, as we will come to talk more about in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 而且他是一位战术大师，我们稍后会详细谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But even with all of that, the idea of going to war with Rome was still a bold move, some might even say reckless.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，与罗马开战的想法依然是一个极其大胆的举动，有些人甚至会说这是鲁莽。

sentences.en: So why did he do it? Most historians believe the plan was not necessarily to destroy Rome completely, or to conquer the city, but rather to regain the territory that Carthage had lost after the first Punic War: specifically, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica.
sentences.zh: 那么他为什么要这么做？大多数历史学家认为，他的计划未必是彻底消灭罗马或征服这座城市，而是要收复迦太基在第一次布匿战争后失去的领土：具体来说，就是西西里岛、撒丁岛和科西嘉岛。

sentences.en: The surest way to do this, Hannibal thought, was to take the fight to the Romans, in Rome.
sentences.zh: Hannibal认为，实现这一目标最稳妥的方法，就是把战火直接烧到罗马人老家——罗马城去。

sentences.en: After a couple of years fighting in Iberia, and then the successful siege of a city that was allied with Rome, a city called Saguntum that’s just north of Valencia, the stage was set.
sentences.zh: 在伊比利亚半岛作战几年，并成功围攻了一座与罗马结盟的城市（位于巴伦西亚正北方的萨古恩图姆）之后，一切条件都成熟了。

sentences.en: In the spring of 218 BCE, Rome declared war on Carthage.
sentences.zh: 公元前218年春，罗马向迦太基宣战。

sentences.en: The only question was, where would the fighting take place?
sentences.zh: 唯一的悬念是，战斗将在哪里打响？

sentences.en: The Carthaginians were in modern-day Spain; the Roman army was in modern-day Italy.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人在今天的西班牙；罗马军队在今天的意大利。

sentences.en: Two Roman legions were sent across the Mediterranean to face Hannibal, but when they arrived, they found that Hannibal had done something they hadn’t bargained for.
sentences.zh: 两个罗马军团被派往地中海迎战Hannibal，但当他们抵达时，发现Hannibal做了他们始料未及的事。

sentences.en: Instead of taking the quickest route, by ship, he had marched his men northwards, up through Spain and southern France.
sentences.zh: 他没有选择坐船走最快的路线，而是率领部下一路向北，穿越西班牙和法国南部。

sentences.en: This Carthaginian force, which included tens of thousands of soldiers, cavalry and war elephants, would march across the Pyrenees mountains, through Gaul [in modern-day France], and over the Alps into northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 这支迦太基军队包括数万名步兵、骑兵和战鹰，他们将翻越比利牛斯山脉，穿过高卢（今法国境内），再翻越阿尔卑斯山进入意大利北部。

sentences.en: And this wasn’t just a ragtag group of Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 这可不是一群乌合之众。

sentences.en: His army was a multi-ethnic coalition: Libyans, Numidians, Iberians, Gauls, and Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他的军队是一个多民族的联合体：利比亚人、努米底亚人、伊比利亚人、高卢人以及迦太基人。

sentences.en: Each group brought different strengths. The Numidians, from what is now Algeria, were exceptional light cavalry — fast, agile, and used to hit-and-run tactics that confused heavier Roman formations.
sentences.zh: 每个族群都带来了不同的优势。来自今阿尔及利亚的努米底亚人是出色的轻骑兵——动作迅捷、灵活，擅长打完就跑的游击战术，常常令笨重的罗马阵型晕头转向。

sentences.en: They didn’t wear armour, rode bareback, and were masters at harassment and retreat, so perfect for skirmishing and flanking.
sentences.zh: 他们不穿盔甲，骑马不配鞍，是骚扰和撤退的大师，非常适合用于小规模冲突和侧翼包抄。

sentences.en: The Libyans were often used as heavy infantry.
sentences.zh: 利比亚人通常被用作重步兵。

sentences.en: Though they were originally supporting troops, many of them had been trained and equipped in the Roman style, with long spears, oval shields, and discipline drilled into them by years of warfare.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们最初只是支援部队，但其中许多人已经接受了罗马风格的训练和装备，配备长矛、椭圆形盾牌，并且经过多年战事的洗礼，纪律严明。

sentences.en: They gave Hannibal a solid, reliable core.
sentences.zh: 他们为Hannibal提供了坚实可靠的中坚力量。

sentences.en: The Iberians, from what is now Spain, were fierce and mobile, and were especially suited to mountainous terrain.
sentences.zh: 来自今西班牙的伊比利亚人凶猛且机动性强，特别适合山地作战。

sentences.en: Their weapon of choice was a curved sword with devastating cutting power.
sentences.zh: 他们首选的武器是一种具有极强切割力的弯刀。

sentences.en: They weren’t as heavily armoured as the Roman troops, but they were bold and adaptable.
sentences.zh: 他们的盔甲没有罗马军队那么厚重，但他们勇敢且适应力极强。

sentences.en: Then there were the Gauls, the recently conquered or allied tribes from southern France.
sentences.zh: 还有高卢人，也就是刚刚被征服或归附的法国南部部落。

sentences.en: They were unpredictable, loud, often drunk and at times undisciplined, but they could bring raw power and overwhelming force when unleashed in a charge.
sentences.zh: 他们变幻莫测、吵闹喧哗、常常喝得酩酊大醉有时甚至缺乏纪律，但在发起冲锋时，他们能爆发出原始的力量和排山倒海的冲击力。

sentences.en: The army was a microcosm of Carthage itself: diverse, pragmatic, and driven by a combination of loyalty to Hannibal and a shared loathing of Rome.
sentences.zh: 这支军队可以说是迦太基自身的缩影：多元、务实，并由对Hannibal的忠诚以及对罗马的共同仇恨结合在一起驱动着。

sentences.en: And, of course, there were the war elephants.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有战象。

sentences.en: Not particularly numerous, but terrifying.
sentences.zh: 数量虽然不多，但极具威慑力。

sentences.en: Roman horses had never seen creatures like these, and neither had most Roman soldiers.
sentences.zh: 罗马的战马从未见过这样的生物，绝大多数罗马士兵也是如此。

sentences.en: The elephants were difficult to control and not always particularly reliable, but their presence caused fear and chaos on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 战象很难控制，也并非总是那么可靠，但它们的存在在战场上引发了极大的恐惧和混乱。

sentences.en: And it was this army that marched through Southern France and crossed the Alps in the summer of 218 BCE.
sentences.zh: 正是这支军队在公元前218年夏天穿过法国南部并翻越了阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: It’s still not clear exactly which route Hannibal took, but there was and still is no easy route across the Alps.
sentences.zh: 目前仍不清楚Hannibal具体走的是哪条路线，但过去和现在都没有一条轻松的路线可以翻越阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: Managing it was a feat so bold that Roman historians centuries later still couldn’t quite believe it had actually happened.
sentences.zh: 能做到这一点是一个如此大胆的壮举，以至于几个世纪后的罗马历史学家仍然不敢相信这一切真的发生过。

sentences.en: The terrain was treacherous, and the weather brutal.
sentences.zh: 这里地形险恶，天气残酷。

sentences.en: They lost thousands of men. The elephants struggled in the snow.
sentences.zh: 他们损失了数千人。大象在雪地里举步维艰。

sentences.en: Hannibal himself is said to have gone blind in one eye from an infection during the crossing.
sentences.zh: 据说Hannibal本人在翻越山脉期间也因感染导致一只眼睛失明。

sentences.en: But against all odds, they made it. And what Hannibal found when he descended into northern Italy was… opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但历经千难万险，他们成功了。当Hannibal率军降临意大利北部时，他发现的是……机遇。

sentences.en: Many of the tribes and cities that had been brought under Roman control were not especially loyal.
sentences.zh: 许多被纳入罗马统治之下的部落和城市其实并不算忠诚。

sentences.en: They resented Roman taxes, Roman military conscription, and Roman interference in local affairs.
sentences.zh: 他们痛恨罗马的税收、罗马的兵役以及罗马对地方事务的干涉。

sentences.en: They would do almost anything to be rid of their oppressor, and Hannibal was ready to take full advantage.
sentences.zh: 为了摆脱压迫者，他们愿意付出一切代价，而Hannibal已经准备好充分利用这一点。

sentences.en: He had no illusions about being able to conquer Rome by himself.
sentences.zh: 他对靠自己一人之力征服罗马并没有抱任何幻想。

sentences.en: His strategy relied on breaking Rome’s alliances, encouraging these Italian communities to join him and rise up against the Republic.
sentences.zh: 他的战略依赖于瓦解罗马的同盟，鼓励这些意大利社区加入他并奋起反抗共和国。

sentences.en: If he could do that, if he could isolate Rome, then maybe, just maybe, it would fall.
sentences.zh: 如果他能做到这一点，如果他能孤立罗马，那么也许，仅仅是也许，它就会垮台。

sentences.en: And the first step in that plan? Win battles.
sentences.zh: 这个计划的第一步是什么？赢得战斗。

sentences.en: Win them quickly, and win them dramatically.
sentences.zh: 速战速决，打出轰动效应。

sentences.en: And that’s exactly what Hannibal did. Now, there have been tens of thousands of pages written about the genius of Hannibal’s military strategy, so if you are a military history buff, you’ll have to excuse the brevity with which we’ll be covering them today.
sentences.zh: 而这正是Hannibal所做的。关于Hannibal军事战略的天才之处，后人已经写下了数万页的篇幅，所以如果你是个军事历史迷，请原谅我们今天要简明扼要地带过了。

sentences.en: The first sensational victory came at the River Trebia in 218 BCE, not long after Hannibal had emerged from the Alps.
sentences.zh: 第一场轰动性的胜利发生在公元前218年的特雷比亚河畔，当时Hannibal刚从阿尔卑斯山出来不久。

sentences.en: A large Roman force was sent up to meet him.
sentences.zh: 罗马派出一支庞大的军队前去迎战。

sentences.en: And just in case you need a reminder, Roman soldiers were incredibly well- drilled and well-trained.
sentences.zh: 为了以防你需要提醒，罗马士兵一向训练有素、纪律严明。

sentences.en: But they were ill-prepared for a master tactician.
sentences.zh: 但他们对一位战术大师却毫无防备。

sentences.en: At Trebia, the Romans assumed Hannibal and his army would be weak, cold, and demoralised after the gruelling crossing.
sentences.zh: 在特雷比亚，罗马人以为Hannibal和他的军队经历艰苦的翻山越岭之后一定虚弱、寒冷且士气低落。

sentences.en: They were wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们想错了。

sentences.en: Hannibal sent his light cavalry to the bank of the river to try to draw the Romans across.
sentences.zh: Hannibal派遣他的轻骑兵到河岸边，试图诱使罗马人渡河。

sentences.en: The Romans took the bait and marched through the freezing river, assuming their superior forces would have no problem defeating the seemingly small number of Hannibal’s cavalry.
sentences.zh: 罗马人上钩了，冒着冰冷的河水蹚了过来，他们自恃兵力雄厚，消灭Hannibal那看似数量不多的骑兵根本不在话下。

sentences.en: Little did the Romans know that it was a trap.
sentences.zh: 罗马人万万没有想到这是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: Hannibal's men, well-rested and hidden in ambush positions, attacked the Romans while they were mid-stream.
sentences.zh: Hannibal养精蓄锐、潜伏在埋伏地点的部下，趁罗马人走到河中央时发起了进攻。

sentences.en: It was a slaughter. The Romans were soaked, shivering, and unorganised.
sentences.zh: 这是一场屠杀。罗马人浑身湿透、瑟瑟发抖且毫无阵型。

sentences.en: Hannibal’s cavalry outflanked them, and a hidden unit he had concealed in nearby reeds attacked from behind.
sentences.zh: Hannibal的骑兵包抄了他们，他藏在附近芦苇丛中的一支隐蔽部队也从后方杀出。

sentences.en: The Roman line collapsed. Thousands were killed or taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 罗马防线崩溃了。数千人战死或被俘。

sentences.en: It was a textbook example of Hannibal’s genius.
sentences.zh: 这是Hannibal军事天才的教科书级范例。

sentences.en: He didn’t just fight. He manipulated. He shaped the battlefield to his advantage.
sentences.zh: 他不只是战斗。他操纵局势。他将战场塑造对自已有利的形态。

sentences.en: He attacked not only the Roman army, but Roman arrogance, their assumption that strength alone would be enough.
sentences.zh: 他攻击的不仅是罗马军队，还有罗马人的傲慢，以及他们认为仅凭力量就足够取胜的自大心理。

sentences.en: The following year, 217 BCE, the Romans sent another army to stop him.
sentences.zh: 第二年，即公元前217年，罗马人派出了另一支军队来阻止他。

sentences.en: This time, they met at Lake Trasimene, in central Italy.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们在意大利中部的特拉西梅诺湖畔相遇了。

sentences.en: Once again, Hannibal lured them into a trap.
sentences.zh: Hannibal故技重施，再次将他们引进了陷阱。

sentences.en: He hid his army in the hills and waited for the perfect moment.
sentences.zh: 他把军队隐藏在群山之中，等待着最佳时机。

sentences.en: As the Roman column marched along a narrow path at the edge of the lake, his troops launched a surprise attack from the high ground.
sentences.zh: 当罗马军队沿着湖边狭窄的小径行军时，他的部队从制高点发起了突袭。

sentences.en: The Romans were trapped: the lake on one side, the hills on the other, and enemy soldiers pouring down upon them.
sentences.zh: 罗马人陷入了绝境：一边是湖水，一边是群山，敌军如潮水般从上方倾泻而下。

sentences.en: It was another massacre.
sentences.zh: 又是一场大屠杀。

sentences.en: Roman sources claim that 15,000 were killed, and another 10,000 captured.
sentences.zh: 据罗马史料记载，有15,000人阵亡，另有10,000人被俘。

sentences.en: It remains one of the largest ambushes in military history, and is quite a testament to Hannibal’s supreme authority and control over his men, men who would have spoken dozens of different languages, and many who would be itching for the chance to avenge murdered loved ones and relatives at the hands of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这依然是军事史上规模最大的伏击战之一，它充分证明了Hannibal对部下的崇高威望和绝对掌控。他的部下说着几十种不同的方言，其中许多人正渴望着为被罗马人杀害的亲人报仇雪恨。

sentences.en: There were something like 40,000 men who lay hidden in the wood above the hills, watching carefully as the Roman army marched far enough past for Hannibal to give the order to finally attack.
sentences.zh: 当时大约有4万名士兵埋伏在山上的树林里，全神贯注地看着罗马军队行进到足够远的位置，直到Hannibal下达最终进攻的命令。

sentences.en: And the result was, well, one of history’s deadliest ambushes, and another devastating loss for Rome.
sentences.zh: 结果正如所料，这是历史上最致命的伏击之一，也是罗马遭遇的又一次毁灭性打击。

sentences.en: Rome, at this point, was in a state of panic.
sentences.zh: 此时的罗马陷入了极度恐慌。

sentences.en: This foreign general had marched across the Alps, destroyed two Roman armies, and was now in the heart of Italy.
sentences.zh: 这位外籍将军翻越阿尔卑斯山，摧毁了两支罗马军队，如今已经逼近意大利腹地。

sentences.en: Whispers began to spread. Would he march on Rome itself?
sentences.zh: 流言四起。他会直接进攻罗马城吗？

sentences.en: But Hannibal didn’t. Not yet. And this decision, perhaps more than any other, has puzzled historians for centuries.
sentences.zh: 但Hannibal没有。至少当时没有。这个决定，也许比其他任何决定都更让历史学家们困惑了几个世纪。

sentences.en: Why didn’t he go straight for Rome? There are a few possible reasons.
sentences.zh: 他为什么不直接攻打罗马？原因有几个。

sentences.en: Firstly, Rome was well fortified. Its walls were high and thick.
sentences.zh: 首先，罗马防御坚固。它的城墙又高又厚。

sentences.en: Hannibal didn’t have the siege equipment to breach them.
sentences.zh: Hannibal没有攻城重型装备来攻破它们。

sentences.en: Secondly, he may have hoped that with enough victories, Rome’s allies would desert it, and the city would collapse from within.
sentences.zh: 其次，他可能希望随着一场场胜利，罗马的同盟会背叛它，从而导致这座城市从内部瓦解。

sentences.en: A siege, he knew, would be long and costly, and his army had never been particularly good at sieges.
sentences.zh: 他深知围城战将旷日持久且代价高昂，而且他的军队向来不擅长攻城。

sentences.en: Ambushes and surprise attacks on the field - that was his thing.
sentences.zh: 伏击和野战突袭才是他的拿手好戏。

sentences.en: And so instead, he continued his campaign through Italy, trying to weaken Roman alliances, break their hold on the peninsula, and draw them into more battles.
sentences.zh: 因此，他转而在意大利继续作战，试图削弱罗马的同盟，打破他们对半岛的控制，并诱使他们进行更多决战。

sentences.en: Which brings us to 216 BCE. To the fields of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了公元前216年。来到了坎尼的原野。

sentences.en: Here, the Romans had had enough. They raised the largest army they had ever assembled.
sentences.zh: 在这里，罗马人忍无可忍了。他们集结了有史以来规模最庞大的军队。

sentences.en: Estimates vary, but some sources suggest up to 80,000 infantry and 6,000 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 估算各不相同，但一些资料显示，他们拥有多达8万名步兵和6万名骑兵。

sentences.en: Two Roman consuls, each commanding half of the force, led them out to finally crush Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 两名罗马执政官各率领一半兵力，出征誓要彻底消灭Hannibal。

sentences.en: Hannibal had perhaps 50,000 men. He was outnumbered nearly 2 to 1.
sentences.zh: 当时Hannibal大约有5万部下。他的兵力处于近乎二比一的劣势。

sentences.en: And yet, he won. Not just won; he annihilated them.
sentences.zh: 然而，他赢了。不仅赢了；而且是全歼。

sentences.en: At Cannae, Hannibal demonstrated perhaps the most perfect example of battlefield strategy in ancient history.
sentences.zh: 在坎尼，Hannibal展示了古代历史上堪称完美的战场战术范例。

sentences.en: He deliberately placed his most lightly-armoured troops, mostly Gauls, whom the Romans viewed as fierce but undisciplined warriors, in the centre of his line.
sentences.zh: 他故意将自己最薄弱的部队——主要是被罗马人视为凶猛但缺乏纪律的高卢人——部署在阵型的中央。

sentences.en: As the Romans advanced, this centre slowly gave ground, forming a crescent, then a sort of half circle.
sentences.zh: 随着罗马军队的推进，这个中心缓缓后撤，形成了一个月牙形，接着变成了一种半圆形的弧度。

sentences.en: To the Romans, it looked like Hannibal was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 在罗马人看来，这像是Hannibal的防线正在崩溃。

sentences.en: So they pushed harder, deeper, funnelling themselves into the curve.
sentences.zh: 于是他们乘胜追击，向更深处推进，成群结队地挤进了这个弧形凹陷中。

sentences.en: Little did they know that that was exactly what Hannibal wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们万万没有想到，这正是Hannibal梦寐以求的。

sentences.en: Once the Romans were surrounded on three sides, his elite African infantry attacked from the sides.
sentences.zh: 一旦罗马人三面受敌，他精锐的非洲步兵便从两侧发起了合围。

sentences.en: His cavalry, having driven off the Roman horsemen, came in from behind.
sentences.zh: 而他的骑兵在击溃了罗马骑兵后，也从后方包抄过来。

sentences.en: The Romans were surrounded in every direction.
sentences.zh: 罗马人四面楚歌。

sentences.en: They couldn’t move. They couldn’t fight; they were too packed together to lift their weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们动弹不得。他们甚至无法战斗，因为挤得太紧连武器都举不起来。

sentences.en: They couldn’t even run. What followed was a killing field.
sentences.zh: 他们连逃跑都做不到。接下来的地方变成了人间炼狱。

sentences.en: Estimates vary wildly, but it’s believed that around 50,000 Roman soldiers were killed in a single day.
sentences.zh: 虽然各方估计悬殊，但据信大约有5万名罗马士兵在短短一天内阵亡。

sentences.en: It was one of the worst defeats in Roman history, and by some measures, more Roman soldiers were being killed per minute than would be by machine guns on the battlefield of the Somme.
sentences.zh: 这是罗马历史上最惨重的失败之一，按某些标准计算，罗马士兵阵亡的速率甚至超过了后来索姆河战役中机枪造成的伤亡。

sentences.en: And still, Hannibal didn’t march on Rome.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，Hannibal依然没有进军罗马。

sentences.en: Why not? Again, we can only speculate. Perhaps he lacked siege equipment.
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？我们依然只能推测。也许是因为缺乏攻城装备。

sentences.en: Perhaps he didn’t believe the city would fall.
sentences.zh: 也许他认为这座城市根本攻不破。

sentences.en: Perhaps he hoped Rome would finally sue for peace.
sentences.zh: 也许他希望罗马最终会求和。

sentences.en: But Rome didn’t. And this is where the tide began to turn.
sentences.zh: 但罗马没有。正是在这里，战局开始逆转。

sentences.en: The Romans changed their strategy. They adopted what became known as the Fabian Strategy, named after the general Quintus Fabius Maximus.
sentences.zh: 罗马人改变了战略。他们采用了后来被称为“费边战略”（Fabian Strategy）的战术，该战术是以将军昆图斯·费边·马克西姆斯（Quintus Fabius Maximus）的名字命名的。

sentences.en: Rather than face Hannibal in open battle, they avoided direct confrontation.
sentences.zh: 他们不再与Hannibal进行正面决战，而是避免直接对抗。

sentences.en: They harassed his supply lines. They wore him down.
sentences.zh: 他们袭扰他的补给线。他们不断消耗他的实力。

sentences.en: Now, Fabius Maximus had been advocating for this strategy since the early Roman defeats, but it was not a popular one with the Roman leadership.
sentences.zh: 其实，费边·马克西姆斯早在罗马遭遇早期惨败时就一直倡导这一战略，但在罗马领导层中它并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Rome was a military power, Romans gained honour and glory in battle, and running away from the battlefield instead of towards it seemed the antithesis of everything Rome stood for.
sentences.zh: 罗马是一个军事强国，罗马人在战场上赢得荣誉与辉煌，而逃避战场而不是迎难而上，似乎与罗马所代表的一切背道而驰。

sentences.en: Yet, after these three catastrophic defeats, it was agreed that perhaps Fabius Maximus might have a point.
sentences.zh: 然而，经历了这三次惨痛的失败后，人们终于一致认为，费边·马克西姆斯也许真的说对了。

sentences.en: Years passed. Hannibal’s army remained in Italy but was fighting a war of attrition.
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝。Hannibal的军队虽然留在了意大利，但陷入了一场旷日持久的消耗战。

sentences.en: The Romans would launch little attacks on parties foraging for food, they would burn fields and crops, and they would do everything they could to make surviving difficult for Hannibal’s forces.
sentences.zh: 罗马人开始对搜寻食物的小股敌军发动袭击，他们烧毁田地和庄稼，竭尽所能让Hannibal的军队难以生存。

sentences.en: As for the Carthaginians, they were far from home, with no reinforcements, no steady supply of men or food.
sentences.zh: 至于迦太基人，他们远离故土，既没有后援，也没有源源不断的兵源和粮食补给。

sentences.en: Hannibal’s initial hope, that Rome’s allies would rise up and join him, had largely not transpired.
sentences.zh: Hannibal最初的希望——即罗马的同盟会起义加入他——大部分并没有实现。

sentences.en: Some did, but most stayed loyal to Rome.
sentences.zh: 虽然有一些人加入了，但大多数人依然对罗马忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: Eventually, Rome took the fight back to Carthage itself.
sentences.zh: 最终，罗马人把战火烧回了迦太基本土。

sentences.en: A seasoned Roman commander, Publius Cornelius Scipio, fresh from victories in Iberia, led a daring campaign in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 一位经验丰富的罗马统帅——刚在伊比利亚取得胜利的普布利乌斯·科尔内利乌斯·西庇阿（Publius Cornelius Scipio），在北非发起了一场大胆的远征。

sentences.en: To counter this threat, and because not much progress was being made in the Italian peninsula, Carthage recalled Hannibal and his forces.
sentences.zh: 为了应对这一威胁，加上在意大利半岛进展不大，迦太基召回了Hannibal及其军队。

sentences.en: And it was there, at the Battle of Zama in 202 BCE, that Hannibal finally met his match.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，在公元前202年的扎马战役中，Hannibal终于遇到了他的克星。

sentences.en: Scipio had studied Hannibal. He knew his tactics, he knew the advantages and disadvantages of his various types of soldiers, and he knew how Hannibal liked to fight.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿研究过Hannibal。他了解他的战术，清楚他麾下各类士兵的优缺点，也摸透了Hannibal惯常的作战风格。

sentences.en: Scipio outmanoeuvred him, used Roman discipline to resist the initial elephant charge, and then exploited gaps in the Carthaginian line.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿技高一筹，利用罗马军队的纪律抵挡住了最初的战象冲锋，随后成功切入了迦太基阵型的漏洞。

sentences.en: Hannibal was defeated, and Carthage was forced to surrender.
sentences.zh: Hannibal战败了，迦太基被迫投降。

sentences.en: Hannibal lived on for another couple of decades.
sentences.zh: Hannibal又活了大约二十年。

sentences.en: He entered politics, tried to reform Carthage, and later went into exile.
sentences.zh: 他投身政治，试图改革迦太基，后来被迫流亡。

sentences.en: He continued to advise other kings and even plotted further campaigns against Rome.
sentences.zh: 他继续为其他君王出谋划策，甚至策划着进一步反抗罗马的战役。

sentences.en: In one display of particularly creative military thinking, in a battle between two naval powers in modern-day Turkey, he advised for poisonous snakes to be put into clay pots and then thrown onto the enemy ship, the logic being that soldiers on ships don’t tend to wear many clothes, and they can’t exactly run away, so having hundreds of angry poisonous snakes slithering around is pretty much any sailor’s worst nightmare.
sentences.zh: 在展示其极具创意的军事思维时，有一次在现代土耳其境内的一场两国海军之战中，他建议将毒蛇装进陶罐里，然后扔到敌舰上。其逻辑是：战舰上的水兵们通常穿得比较少，而且在船上也无处可逃，因此有成百上千条愤怒的毒蛇在身边滑来滑去，绝对是任何水手挥之不去的噩梦。

sentences.en: Now, despite the fact that he had been exiled from Carthaginian society, Rome never forgot him.
sentences.zh: 尽管他后来被迦太基社会流放，但罗马人从未忘记他。

sentences.en: They pursued him across the Mediterranean, determined to stamp out the threat once and for all.
sentences.zh: 他们在整个地中海对穷追不舍，决心一劳永逸地根除这个威胁。

sentences.en: Eventually, cornered in what is now modern-day Turkey, and with Roman forces bearing down on him, Hannibal took poison rather than be captured.
sentences.zh: 最终，在今天的土耳其境内被逼入绝境、罗马军队步步紧逼之际，Hannibal服毒自尽，拒绝被俘。

sentences.en: His last words are said to have been: “Let us now relieve the Romans from the fear which has long disturbed them.”
sentences.zh: 据说他的遗言是：“让我们为罗马人解除长久以来的恐惧吧。”

sentences.en: He was 64 years old. And yet, more than two thousand years later, the fear he inspired, the brilliance he displayed, the legacy he left behind… it still lingers.
sentences.zh: 他享年64岁。然而，两千多年过去了，他激发出的恐惧、他展现出的才华、他留下的传奇……依然历久弥新，萦绕不散。

sentences.en: Hannibal didn’t destroy Rome. But he very nearly did.
sentences.zh: Hannibal没有毁灭罗马。但他差一点就成功了。

sentences.en: And in so doing, he showed the world what a determined, brilliant mind could achieve with limited resources, a deep sense of purpose, and an oath made as a child that he never forgot.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他向世界展示了一个坚忍不拔、才华横溢的头脑，凭借有限的资源、坚定的信念以及儿时许下且永不忘却的誓言，究竟能成就何等伟业。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于Hannibal的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: If you are interested, there are some really good videos about these battles on YouTube, with all sorts of people recreating them in astonishing detail, so if that sounds like your kind of thing, just search for Hannibal on YouTube and you’ll find some good stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果你感兴趣的话，YouTube上有一些关于这些战役的精彩视频，各种各样的人以惊人的细节重现了这些战斗，如果你喜欢这类内容，只需在YouTube上搜索“Hannibal”，就能找到不少好东西。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你一直在收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
